introduction: This level covers the complex life cycles of protozoa, fungal skin infections, and the science of the immune system that makes vaccines work.

core_concepts.title: Protozoan Diseases
core_concepts.description:
1. Malaria: Pathogen - 'Plasmodium'. Vector - 'Female Anopheles'. Affected Organs - 'Liver, Spleen, and RBCs'. Medicine: **Quinine** (extracted from the bark of the Cinchona tree). 
2. Kala-azar (Black Fever): Pathogen - 'Leishmania'. Vector - 'Sandfly'. 
3. Sleeping Sickness: Pathogen - 'Trypanosoma'. Vector - 'Tsetse fly'.

core_concepts.title: Fungal Diseases
core_concepts.description:
Fungi thrive in warm, moist environments and primarily cause 'Skin' infections. 
Examples: 
1. Ringworm: Causes round, red, itchy, and scaly patches on the skin. 
2. Athlete's Foot: A fungal infection specifically between the toes. 
3. Asthma (Certain types): Triggered by inhaling fungal spores into the lungs.

core_concepts.title: The Immune System: Antigen vs. Antibody
core_concepts.description:
1. Antigen: Any 'foreign substance' (like a viral protein or bacteria) that enters the body and triggers an immune response. 
2. Antibody: The 'protein weapons' produced by our own White Blood Cells (B-cells) to lock onto and destroy specific antigens.

core_concepts.title: The Principle of Vaccination
core_concepts.description:
A vaccine actually contains a **'Weakened or Dead Pathogen'**. When injected, it doesn't make us sick, but it tricks our immune system into thinking there is an attack. The body produces **'Antibodies'** against it and creates 'Memory Cells'. If the real, strong virus ever attacks in the future, the memory cells instantly kill it. 
Edward Jenner discovered the very first vaccine (for Smallpox).

important_entities.name: The Life Cycle of Malaria
important_entities.significance: The Malaria parasite (Plasmodium) is unique; it requires TWO hosts to complete its life cycle: 1. Humans (where it bursts RBCs causing high fever chills) and 2. The Female Anopheles Mosquito (where it reproduces).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Because of the word 'worm' in its name, students often classify it as a disease caused by worms (like Ascaris or Tapeworm). Remember, 'Ringworm' is strictly a **Fungal** skin infection. There is no worm involved!

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Malaria, Kala-azar (Kids), Sleeping Sickness (Sleep). All are caused by Protozoa.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite NDA/CDS question: 'The anti-malarial drug Quinine is obtained from which plant?' Answer: The bark of the Cinchona tree.
